sections.h2: Where Mackinac County deeds get filed
sections.html:
The county's Register of Deeds works from the first floor of the Mackinac County Courthouse at 100 S. Marley in St. Ignace. The phone line is (906) 643-7306. The County Treasurer is one floor up (second floor, Room 30, phone (906) 643-7318), and the Equalization Department sits in the Courthouse Annex, Room 120, at (906) 643-7310. A seller who needs a deed filed, a tax certificate and a parcel record can finish all three errands in one courthouse complex.

Mackinac County is spread across the Straits of Mackinac, with 1,079 of its 2,101 square miles in the lake and 10,834 residents at the 2020 census. St. Ignace is the seat and Mackinac Island is the other city. Owners who live far from the courthouse should use the mail or e-recording options below.

sections.h2: Can a deed be sent by mail or e-recording?
sections.html:
Yes to both. Nobody has to appear in person, and documents with the right fee can go by mail, UPS or FedEx. Electronic filers can route through CSC E-Recording Solutions, Simplifile or EPN E Recording Partners Network, each with its own price list.

Staff offer a service most counties skip: they will look over a draft before you submit it. The office cannot write a private legal document or advise you, but it will check a draft against the recording rules. That can save a round trip across the Straits. A few handy points:

  • Include a self-addressed return envelope so the original comes back sooner.
  • In a deed the grantor is the seller and the grantee is the buyer.
  • Copy the legal description from the prior deed or a new survey, and avoid the shortened version printed on a tax statement unless someone has verified it.
  • Blanket assignments and blanket releases are accepted.
  • Forms are sold at office supply stores or available online, and a local title company may supply one.

Before you send anything, call (906) 643-7306 to confirm the total. Put the deed, the fee check and the return envelope in one package, and keep a note of the date you mailed it so you can follow up if the recorded copy is slow to come back.

One flat charge covers a document of any length. Under MCL 600.2567 that is $30.00, in force since October 1, 2016, and $4 of it goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund. A deed with a warranty clause also needs a treasurer's certificate for $5.00, and the register suggests a single $35.00 check. If you mail the deed, its staff pick up the certificate for you.

Mackinac County Register of Deeds charges

A certified copy must reproduce the whole document. Michigan's registers of deeds pushed in 2016 to stop private companies from selling deeds to residents at inflated prices, so compare any mailer against the office's own rate above.

sections.h2: Transfer tax for a Mackinac County seller
sections.html:
Seller-side transfer tax runs $4.30 for every $500 of price, rounded up for any leftover amount. That is the county's 55 cents (MCL 207.504) plus the state's $3.75. The statute puts the burden on the grantor.

The deed must state the full price on its face, or a valuation affidavit goes with it at no filing charge, and the deed must say the affidavit is attached. Tax stamps are bought where the land sits, and land in two counties needs a stated split.

Exemptions appear on the register's county and state exemption pages and in MCL 207.526. Gifts to children and grandchildren, foreclosure transfers and court-ordered transfers are among them. An exemption has to be written on the face of the deed, so settle it with your closing agent before signing.

Ask your closing agent to show the transfer tax line on the settlement statement ahead of time. It is a seller cost, so it comes out of your proceeds at the table, and it is paid when the deed is filed.

sections.h2: If the house is behind on a mortgage or taxes
sections.html:
Mackinac County's register and treasurer jointly run a foreclosure prevention page, and it explains a ranking that surprises many owners: a tax foreclosure takes precedence over a mortgage foreclosure. Once a mortgage foreclosure starts, the owner keeps control of the property for 6 months, or 12 months if the parcel is larger than 3 acres, and can refinance or sell during that time.

The page also offers a set of practical steps:

  • Call the lender early and read every letter it sends.
  • Look for a HUD-approved housing counselor, since counseling is free or low cost.
  • Contact the Michigan State Housing Development Authority about its Save the Dream program.
  • Do not pay a company that promises to stop a foreclosure, and never sign a paper that appoints someone to act for you.

On the tax side, the County Treasurer collects delinquent property taxes for the local units and handles the summer auction of foreclosed properties under Public Act 123. The Equalization Department hosts a property and delinquent tax search and a list of each local unit's assessor and treasurer. A sale that pays off the balance before the redemption window ends is one way out.

sections.h2: What a recorded deed changes for property tax
sections.html:
The register notifies the assessor of recorded transfers each month, and the new owner must also file with the local assessor within 45 days under MCL 211.27a. A transfer of ownership resets the following year's taxable value to the state equalized value. Moves to a spouse, and residential moves to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild with no commercial use, do not count.

A rental of fewer than 15 days in a year counts as non-commercial, which matters for a cottage that sees a few weekend guests. Longer rentals fall outside that carve-out. Ask the assessor for the parcel's current taxable value before you list.

The register also processes passport applications Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., which helps a relocating seller who needs travel documents at the same visit.

Keep the recorded deed with your closing papers. If a buyer later files the transfer notice late, the assessor may contact the new owner first, but your own records show when title passed.

faqs.q: Is it $30 or $35 to file a deed in Mackinac County?
faqs.a: It is $35.00 when the deed contains a warranty clause, made up of the $30.00 filing fee and the $5.00 treasurer's certificate, and $30.00 when it does not. Each extra instrument released in one document adds $3.00.

faqs.q: Who writes the deed for a Mackinac County sale?
faqs.a: A title company or attorney should draft it. Register staff cannot draft private legal documents, though they will review a draft for compliance with the recording rules before you submit it.

faqs.q: What is the combined transfer tax rate for a Mackinac County home?
faqs.a: The combined rate is $4.30 per $500 of price or fraction, made up of 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state. The grantor pays it.

faqs.q: Who runs the foreclosure auction in Mackinac County?
faqs.a: The County Treasurer, at 100 S. Marley, Room 30, handles the summer auction of foreclosed properties. Call (906) 643-7318, or use the property and delinquent tax search on the Equalization Department page.

faqs.q: How long can an owner stay after a Mackinac County mortgage foreclosure begins?
faqs.a: Six months, or twelve months if the parcel has more than 3 acres. During that window the owner can refinance or sell.
